issue: Ordinary fruit touches can be discarded after a small finger movement, even when release remains inside the same fruit.

confirmedMechanism.previousHandler: CollectItem bound InputMono, which registers drag handlers even though fruits have no drag action.
confirmedMechanism.failure: UGUI marks the touch as dragging after the threshold. InputMono.OnPointerClick then rejects the click.
confirmedMechanism.baselineReproducedInUnity: Stationary touch invokes InputMono; moving 15 pixels within its Image before release does not.

fix.input: Prefab-owned FruitCollectButton derives from standard Unity UI Button and sits on the existing visible fruit Image.
fix.binding: Code binds onClick and Selectable-state animation feedback. No persistent Inspector event or runtime-created input component.
preserved: Same fruit visual and raycast rectangle
Pressed and released fruit animation feedback
Symmetric pool and undo event binding

verification.method: Saved fruit prefab, real GraphicRaycaster, original UGUI touch/drag/release dispatch in an isolated Editor fixture.
verification.limits: Positive checks count Button events rather than initializing gameplay storage. Negative checks retain the production callback. Binding idempotence is reviewed statically; no private listener count is inspected.

deviceVerification.reason: The user switched the phone to another application during investigation; further phone interaction was stopped.

conclusion: A real normal-play input defect has been reproduced and corrected in the project. This does not establish that every historical missed touch had this cause.
